questions.text:
There are two elements x,y in a group (G,*) such that every element in the group can be written as a product of some number of x's and y's in some order. It is known that
x * x = y * y = x * y *x * y = y* x * y *x = e
where e is the identity element. The maximum number of elements in such a group is _______.
questions.solution:
[latex]x^2=y^2=e[/latex] and [latex](xy)^2=e[/latex] give [latex]xy=(xy)^{-1}=y^{-1}x^{-1}=yx[/latex], so x and y commute.

Every product then reduces to one of e, x, y, xy (the Klein four-group).

Answer: 4

questions.text:
Consider the set of all functions f:{0,1,...,2014}[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]{0,1...,2014} such that f(f(i))=i, for 0[latex]\leq[/latex]i[latex]\leq[/latex]2014 . Consider the following statements.
P. For each such function it must be the case that for every i, f(i) = i,
Q. For each such function it must be the case that for some i,f(i) = i,
R. Each such function must be onto.
Which one of the following is CORRECT?
questions.solution:
f(f(i)) = i means f is its own inverse, so f is a bijection [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] R true.

- P false: f can swap pairs, e.g. f(0) = 1, f(1) = 0.
- Q true: f splits the 2015 elements into fixed points and swapped pairs. 2015 is odd, so at least one fixed point exists.

Answer: Only Q and R are true

options: P, Q and R are true
Only Q and R are true
Only P and Q are true

questions.text: Let S be a sample space and two mutually exclusive events A and B be such that A[latex]\cup[/latex]B = S. If P(.) denotes the probability of the event, the maximum value of P(A)P(B) is ______
questions.solution:
Mutually exclusive and union = S, so P(A) + P(B) = 1.

P(A)(1 [latex]-[/latex] P(A)) is maximum at P(A) = 0.5, giving 0.5 [latex]\times[/latex] 0.5 = 0.25.

Answer: 0.25

questions.text: Suppose depth first search is executed on the graph below starting at some unknown vertex. Assume that a recursive call to visit a vertex is made only after first checking that the vertex has not been visited earlier. Then the maximum possible recursion depth (including the initial call) is _________.
questions.solution:
Max recursion depth = number of vertices on the longest simple path DFS can follow.

- Left 3 [latex]\times[/latex] 3 grid: a snake path covers all 9 vertices, ending at its bottom-right corner.
- Bottom middle vertex: 1 (its pendant above is a dead end, so skip it).
- Right 3 [latex]\times[/latex] 3 grid: enter at the bottom-left corner; we must end at the middle-right vertex to reach the pendant. A grid is bipartite (5 corner-coloured, 4 other), so a corner-to-middle path can cover only 8 vertices.
- Right pendant: 1

Depth = 9 + 1 + 8 + 1 = 19

Answer: 19

questions.text: Let G be a group with 15 elements. Let L be a subgroup of G. It is known that L[latex]\neq[/latex]G and that the size of L is at least 4. The size of L is _______.
questions.solution:
By Lagrange's theorem, |L| divides 15, so |L| is 1, 3, 5 or 15.

L [latex]\ne[/latex] G rules out 15, and [latex]|L|\ge4[/latex] rules out 1 and 3.

Answer: 5
